summary: Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including Khamdre Shedra. He taught at Southwest Minzu University, the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and the University of Naples.

Nancy E. Levine is an anthropologist and Tibetologist. She served as an Associate Professor of anthropology at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she is attested as Professor of anthropology in 2026.

Nancy G. Lin specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She completed graduate studies at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, later serving as faculty at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Nancy Hock specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams and was affiliated with the Asian Art Museum in 1987.

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held an appointment at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies.
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé was a traditional scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indologist and archaeologist. He served as a Superintendent in the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and later as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum.
Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who worked as a visiting scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies and served as an assistant and lecturer at Tohoku University before becoming a professor at Koyasan University.
Naoki Nabeshima specializes in Buddhist studies. As attested in 2004, he founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies.
Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD at Tohoku University between 1993 and 2002 under doctoral supervisor Toshifumi Goto and later served there as a researcher.

Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford, was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University, and became a professor and co-director at the University of Edinburgh.
Naomichi Nakada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya and doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo, professor at Keio University, and director of Toyo Bunko.

Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions as a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and was affiliated with Otani University in 1981.

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. Educated at St. Benedict's College and University College in Colombo, he served as Superior of Vajirarama in Colombo from around 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (1924–2013) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Delhi under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University from ~1959 to 1984.
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indologist. He served as the librarian (adhyakṣa) at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1932) and later as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
